correctness.rationale: For a unit-circumradius hexagon, the six projected vertices at ±A, ±B, ±C, with A=B+C, yield a central cap, quadrilateral cap and triangular cap. The cap formulas agree at switching surfaces. The change u=sqrt(3)tan(theta) reduces angular minimization to derivative signs in the three valid regimes; the quadrilateral switching function T(u) decreases strictly, and the triangle derivative changes sign at the second oblique branch. Evaluating these exact minimizers gives all four stated normalized area fractions and the two distinct strictly oblique width intervals. Centering follows from even concave section lengths. The existing general planar partial-plank theorem justifies reducing arbitrary finite plank families to one width-W plank; it is not newly proved here. At the three transition widths the formulas and minimizing normal agree. No claim is made that every optimal multi-plank family is a singleton.
risks: Scope: exact unit-circumradius regular hexagon and widths 0<W<sqrt(3), not arbitrary convex hexagons or all tied multi-plank families.
